approach.method_basis: The Parent breeds fresh molecular graphs from accepted, score-ranked survivors using fragment crossover and local atom or bond edits. A fingerprint Gaussian process learned from all earlier accepted scores selects each evaluation batch by correlated posterior draws over the fresh pool. The Parent also verifies stable canonical identities before pool admission, normalizing confirmed aliases without replacing the checked graph. Its bond-change move alters bond order; it has no direct move that shifts an intact side group to a neighboring aromatic position while keeping the whole molecule's composition.
approach.novelty: Add intact pendant-branch relocation to the existing bond-change menu: detach an acyclic side group from an aromatic carbon and reconnect that same group to an adjacent aromatic carbon bearing a hydrogen. This exposes substitution-position alternatives while preserving the group, ring framework and formula. Earlier siblings changed parent allocation or survival, protected all first-parent rings, redirected halogen growth, protected carbonyl atoms, or stabilized identity keys. None tested this positional move in their fresh graph pools. A different graph-walk lineage evaluated ten such moves but retained none; this experiment tests whether the Parent's existing learned pool selection can put a useful positional alternative into accepted breeding ancestry.

hypothesis: Extend the existing change_bond menu with relocation of an intact single-attachment acyclic branch from an aromatic carbon to an adjacent hydrogen-bearing aromatic carbon, exposing positional isomers to the inherited fresh-pool selector while preserving the branch, ring framework and molecular formula.

finding_summary.headline: Positional moves reached useful breeding ancestry, but the panel score fell slightly
finding_summary.insights:
The fresh-pool selector and accepted-survivor breeder can carry a useful positional edit into later ancestry, resolving the earlier graph-walk experiment's absence of retained relocation winners. The demonstrated benefit is narrow: two of 13 evaluated one-atom moves improved their parents, while none of seven evaluated multi-atom moves did. Keeping a larger branch intact therefore establishes access to positional alternatives without establishing better scores. A score-neutral methyl relocation also entered extensive later ancestry, so immediate parent improvement and later usefulness are different observations.

Two final-best molecules have recorded relocation ancestry, but subsequent edits and crossover prevent assigning their endpoint gains to a conserved moved group. Changing the option menu also changes the search path, so the paired panel measures the complete method; it supplies no scores for unselected alternatives. The molecular assessment still finds concentrated aromatic polycycles, reactive heteroatom bonds, strained ring arrangements and unspecified stereochemistry. Local formula and ring conservation did not resolve those chemical limitations, and the panel loss leaves the registered score-benefit expectation refuted even though construction, evaluated positional access and useful breeding ancestry are confirmed.
finding_summary.results:
All 368 sampled branch reconnections preserved the registered atom and bond counts, molecular formula, branch composition and aromatic ring framework. Of the 365 moves that changed molecular identity, 362 reached pools and 20 were evaluated with the relocated attachment still present. The evaluated set contained 13 one-atom and seven multi-atom branches. Two moves beat their generating parents; both moved fluorine. Sixteen evaluated products survived their batch, and 14 were chosen as breeding parents 979 times across 972 later attempts. One fluorine shift increased its source score from 0.382775 to 0.394039, raised the incumbent, and was reused in 444 attempts with 85 later accepted descendants. Every evaluated multi-atom move scored below its best generating parent.

Mean final-best score across three seeds was 0.542797, versus 0.544374 for the Parent: a paired change of -0.001577, which misses the required +0.002 gain. Seed variation decreased from a population standard deviation of 0.013310 to 0.004718, but the paired seed changes were mixed. All 435 pools filled to 160 candidates and all 4,350 proposed evaluations were accepted. Stable identity bookkeeping was preserved; its inherited guard rejected seven unstable representations before pool admission.

molecular.headline: Aromatic polycycles and halogenated amines dominate; reactive bonds, strained ring closures and unspecified stereochemistry persist.
molecular.overall_character: All supplied current and Parent trajectories were read; no objective lacks trajectories. Each current task digest covers 900 recorded molecules, including 870 optimizer proposals. The output contains substantial aromatic and heteroaromatic ring systems, carbonyl-rich aza rings, halogenated aryl groups, saturated amines, and seed-dependent fused or bridged families. Ring-closure text rates range from 0.9736 to 0.9931 and aromatic-atom presence rates from 0.8966 to 0.9862. These are fractions of proposal strings containing those features, not atom fractions or measured ring counts. Charged and stereocentre text rates are 0.0 throughout. Neutral strings nevertheless contain potentially basic amines, and graph inspection identifies unassigned stereocentres in several leading products. There is moderate diversity across the complete panel, with much narrower families within individual seeds and their high-scoring excerpts. Familiar medicinal fragments coexist with heteroatom-halogen bonds, peroxide or N-O linkages, unusual small ring annulations, crowded aminal centres, and occasional extensive duplication of ring systems. Compared with Parent n-213e85380e04, the leading chemotypes have changed, but these broad chemical liabilities remain. Synthetic plausibility is questionable rather than uniformly absent: plausible substructures do not establish a route to each full structure, its stability, or its stereochemistry. The comparisons below use recorded molecule-score associations only. They do not identify an unseen target structure, establish experimental activity, or attribute changes to the algorithm mechanism.

per_task.generated_character: The better products are compact multi-ring molecules with small alkyl substituents and a separate aryl or pyridyl surface. One family retains indole carboxanilide or N-hydroxyamide chemistry; another combines a nitrile, hydroxymethyl ether, fluoropyridyl appendage and a fused unsaturated carbocycle or imine ring. The leading molecule has an O/N-containing benzofused ring, an annulated unsaturated four-membered carbocycle, and an aryl N-formyl substituent carrying an N-S-F connection. The higher cyano/imine examples also contain a four-membered fused ring. Mean proposal SMILES length is 44.7, with ring-closure presence 0.9828, aromatic presence 0.9747 and halogen presence 0.8632. The small fragments are outliers, not the dominant output. The Parent led with a bridged aromatic ketone/fluoropyridyl family; the current leading structures retain comparable compact aromatic character while redistributing the polar groups and ring connectivity. Neither set establishes routine synthesis for its unusual core.
liabilities: The leading N-S-F connection, an N-fluorinated heteroaromatic analogue, and N-O-rich variants deserve separate chemical scrutiny; they are not ordinary aryl fluorination.
The fused unsaturated four-membered rings impose geometric and synthetic constraints despite their valid molecular representations.
Late products can either lose almost the entire substantial scaffold or concatenate it into much larger low-scoring assemblies.
missing_features: The very small low-scoring products lack the combined aromatic surfaces, compact scaffold and distributed polar groups present in the better products; the very large repeated products fail to retain that compact arrangement.

The high-scoring excerpt provides limited chemically routine alternatives preserving these spatial relationships without short unsaturated ring annulations or unusual heteroatom bonds. The scores do not identify an additional mandatory target-specific group.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial methoxy-rich indole carboxanilide scores 0.3051048083696145. The leading annulated aryl/formamide product scores 0.4567167360350841, while two differently connected cyano/imine/fluoropyridyl products both score 0.4423126980074005. The brominated and chlorinated N-hydroxyamide congeners also have the same recorded score, 0.42927028031283077. These examples support a compact aromatic/polar-group arrangement without identifying a uniquely required carbonyl, nitrile or halogen. Hydrogen peroxide, molecular fluorine and the small cyclic peroxide each score 0.0. At the opposite size extreme, a late concatenated cyano/heteroaryl product scores 4.0536924658459062e-22 despite repeating features present in better molecules. The Parent seed-0 leading ketone scored 0.4463521672202675; the changed leading chemistry does not establish that the new N-S-F linkage or small ring is independently beneficial.

per_task.generated_character: The output is dominated by aromatic, nitrogen-rich carbonyl heterocycles, frequently joined to more aromatic rings or repeated heterocyclic units. The leading compact family carries a diaryl thioketone connection, aza-heteroaromatic rings, short O-containing annulation, an N-fluoromethyl substituent and a fused dicarbonyl core. Another high-scoring family is much larger and more planar-looking, combining several aryl/heteroaryl units, a conjugated polyene, nitroso groups, multiple carbonyls and sometimes a carboxyl O-Cl group. The Parent also had mean SMILES length 94.4, but its leading family used linked carbonyl heteroaromatics with an NH connection and peroxide-halogen decoration. Large aromatic assemblies and chemically questionable peripheral groups persist despite the different leading cores.
liabilities: Carboxyl O-Cl groups and N-O-F, N-Cl and N-Br connections raise reactivity concerns independently of their recorded scores.

Nitroso substituents, long unsaturated chains, thioketones and short O/N annulations create distinct stability or synthetic challenges; their coexistence should not be conflated with ordinary carbonyl heterocycle chemistry.
Extensive aromatic repetition and unspecific alkene or ring stereochemistry complicate interpretation of the whole molecules.
missing_features: Low-scoring tiny fragments lack the distributed aromatic surfaces and carbonyl/heteroatom pattern present in the better molecules.

Chemically ordinary peripheral alternatives are inadequately represented in the leading excerpt. The methyl ester demonstrates that an O-Cl linkage is unnecessary for its observed score, but the trajectories do not establish a missing target scaffold.
The bulky repeated families do not demonstrate a broad set of compact, synthetically straightforward cores retaining their useful polar/aromatic pattern.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial aryl-substituted dicarbonyl heterocycle scores 0.548381482770623. The leading thioketone/aza-ring assembly scores 0.6019680938545036, and the much larger nitroso/polyene assembly scores 0.601485552592915. Small chlorine, fluoramine, molecular chlorine and ethane examples all score 0.5; this floor does not show useful recognition features. A matched large-molecule comparison has exactly the same score, 0.6013814616755793, for the methyl carboxylate and its carboxyl O-Cl analogue. The score therefore supplies no favorable evidence for that reactive O-Cl substitution. The higher scores associate with combined aromatic/heterocyclic and carbonyl-rich feature sets, but the similar scores across markedly different sizes do not isolate a size preference. The Parent leading linked heterocycle scored 0.6324703199409752; that higher value also occurred in chemically problematic material.

per_task.generated_character: The better molecules already contain abundant amine chemistry. The leading family combines halogenated aryl surfaces, a saturated diaza ring around a crowded aminal centre, an annulated sulfur-containing ring, and a secondary benzylic amine connection. The top example also bears phenol, methoxy and bromomethyl groups. Neighboring high products contain sulfur-imine or exocyclic sulfur-carbon double-bond representations. Another seed ends with flexible polyamines linking substituted aromatic ends and sulfur-nitrogen groups rather than the same rigid polycycle. Mean proposal SMILES length is 64.9, ring-closure presence 0.9931, aromatic presence 0.9862 and halogen presence 0.9908. The Parent likewise reached high scores with aryl-rich saturated aza rings and aminal or spiro frameworks; the current leading sulfur-containing polycycles change the topology without resolving crowded centres or stereochemical ambiguity.
liabilities: Crowded aminal centres and multiply connected aza/sulfur rings require deliberate synthesis and stability assessment.
Bromomethyl substituents, aryl thiols, sulfur-imine variants and unusual exocyclic S=C graphs are chemically distinct liabilities despite similar high scores.
Flexible polyamine tails can introduce many conformational and protonation possibilities, while the reported SMILES give no explicit charged or stereochemical alternatives.
missing_features: The lower-scoring small molecules do not preserve the aromatic-surface/amine/spacing combination expressed by the better assemblies. Basic ring nitrogens are already present and are not a general missing capability here.
Leading substituted aminal and benzylic centres lack stereochemical specification. Their spatial alternatives are not explicitly represented in the emitted strings.

The neutrally encoded amines do not document alternative protonation states in the proposals. The trajectory alone cannot establish how the downstream evaluator treated protonation or whether different emitted states would change scores.

A related sulfur-imine/ethyl-side-chain structure scores 0.9915177360424775. A much smaller aryl thioester scores 0.0003638537884276605, an arylacetic acid 0.0019285354743598007, and a truncated halogenated benzylic amine 0.0023340911480993214. Thus the visible high-score association is the combination of substantial aromatic surfaces, available amine functionality and connecting geometry; the mere presence of an amine or halogen is insufficient. The final flexible aryl/polyamine/sulfur-imine product can still score 0.9571289553568425, so the exact rigid sulfur-containing core is not uniquely supported. per_task.generated_character: The better molecules are medium-sized, fused nitrogen-containing polycycles combining a benzofused carbonyl heterocycle with an N-methylated larger aza ring. Several contain a seven-membered diaza ring, a cyclic urea-like carbonyl/[nH] unit, and variable additional amide carbonyls. The leading molecule additionally carries a compact chorded carbon bicycle represented with aromatic atoms and two fused four-membered rings; it should not be described as an ordinary phenyl substituent. The Parent leading family combined a pyridyl appendage, carbonyl heterocycle and larger aza-ring connection. The current leading family is differently annulated, but both remain concentrated in coupled aromatic/carbonyl/cyclic-nitrogen chemistry.

N-O-containing carbonyl rings and late peroxide substitution are different from conventional lactam or cyclic urea chemistry and warrant separate scrutiny.
Additional fusion and larger aza-ring closures change conformation and synthetic accessibility together; text uniqueness is not evidence of useful scaffold diversity.

The leading excerpt offers limited ordinary scaffold alternatives preserving this polar-group arrangement without short carbon-bicycle closures or elaborate O/N annulation. A less exotic high-scoring aza/carbonyl example is present, so such closures are not universally required.
Complex substituted and bridged alternatives do not provide explicit stereochemical assignments; the score data do not identify a required unvisited target scaffold.

The current score range remains compatible with multiple related ring arrangements rather than uniquely identifying the unusual small-ring substituent as required.

per_task.generated_character: The leading products are compact fluorinated aza/carbonyl heterocycles bearing an alkenyl ether and an aldehyde-substituted carbocycle. The highest molecule has an N-fluorinated ring nitrogen, an exocyclic N-fluoro imine and a substituted fluorocyclobutane; nearby products have an imino NH and an unsaturated five-membered carbocycle. Another high family combines fluorinated unsaturated oxygen rings with N-formyl, urea-like and amidine/imine connections. The best excerpt has imines and amidic nitrogens but lacks the pendant primary aliphatic amine prominent in the Parent leading aryl/dicarbonyl family. Mean proposal SMILES length is 53.6, ring-closure presence 0.9736, aromatic presence 0.8966 and halogen presence 0.7425. Its carbonyls and fluoroalkyl chemistry are recognizable components, but N-F bonds, aldehydes, enol ethers and densely substituted small rings make the complete products less routine. Chemically stable alternatives to N-fluorinated imine or ring-nitrogen substitution, and explicit stereochemical alternatives for the substituted carbocycles, are poorly represented among the leading products. No unseen target-specific group can be inferred with certainty.

The observed gradient therefore distinguishes compact substitution/polarity combinations sharply and does not reward simply adding more carbonyls or repeating the core. The Parent leading aminomethyl/fluorinated-aryl/dicarbonyl molecule scored 0.5845583988949146. Its primary-amine arrangement is absent from the current leading excerpt, but these different scaffolds do not isolate an amine-addition effect.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The cited high-scoring structures contain N-F, imine N-F, N-Cl/N-Br, O-Cl, N-O-F and N-S-F connections. A methyl ester and its carboxyl O-Cl analogue have the identical recorded score 0.6013814616755793, so feedback does not always distinguish an ordinary peripheral group from a reactive alternative.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not reliably distinguish ordinary carbon-bound halogens from reactive heteroatom-halogen chemistry.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Expose chemically ordinary substitutions that preserve the surrounding scaffold and polar-group role while distinguishing the atom and bond context of a halogen edit. Treat stability-aware alternatives as a generator capability to test, without assuming that a generic halogen removal increases score.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The digest includes late repeated-core products at 4.0536924658459062e-22 and 3.061073839484404e-28 while their compact related families reach 0.4423126980074005 and 0.5021772038235389. Another output has mean SMILES length 94.4 and maximum 247, showing that large assemblies remain accessible; these are string lengths, not molecular weights.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not consistently preserve compact feature arrangements when it combines substantial ring systems.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Provide connected scaffold recombination and simplification options that retain useful aromatic/polar-group arrangements without automatically duplicating large cores. Adapt size changes to observed feedback rather than imposing a universal preferred size.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Higher-scoring excerpts include fused unsaturated four-membered rings, a chorded carbon bicycle with fused four-membered rings, short O/N annulations, and crowded aminal polycycles. Less exotic aza/carbonyl and aryl/amine structures also receive high recorded scores, so these unusual closures are not a demonstrated general requirement.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator offers limited routine ring-topology alternatives within several of its leading chemical families.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Make accessible ring-framework alternatives that retain approximate substituent spacing and functional-group identity without introducing short strained closures. Assess geometry and synthetic interpretability alongside graph validity; more rings or more distinct strings alone do not establish useful coverage.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Every task has stereocentre text rate 0.0. The cited leading aminal/benzylic-amine molecules and aldehyde-substituted cyclobutane molecules contain unassigned tetrahedral centres on direct graph inspection, and unsaturated side chains also lack specified geometric alternatives.
transferable_gaps.gap: The emitted chemistry does not demonstrate explicit stereochemical exploration of its substituted saturated and bridged structures.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Retain chemically meaningful stereochemical annotations and make bounded, valid stereoisomer alternatives accessible when edits create or preserve stereogenic centres. The current observations establish a coverage gap, not a measured score benefit from assigning a particular stereoisomer.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Every task has charged text rate 0.0 despite cited secondary amines, tertiary cyclic amines, flexible polyamines and imine/amidine-like groups. Thus the missing representation capability is not a universal absence of nitrogen or potentially basic centres.
transferable_gaps.gap: The emitted structures do not document chemically justified alternative ionization states for the amines they already contain.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Represent and preserve plausible ionization alternatives in a chemically controlled way when relevant functional groups are present. Establish how those alternatives relate to downstream normalization before assuming the neutral proposal strings imply missing evaluator protonation or a score penalty.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The Parent leading compact fluorinated aryl/dicarbonyl family contained a pendant primary amine; the current corresponding leading excerpt instead concentrates on aldehyde-bearing carbocycles, imines and N-F groups. Elsewhere, conventional methyl ester chemistry and reactive O-Cl chemistry share the same score, while multiple seed-specific high families remain recognizable variants of their own unusual core.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not consistently retain distinct useful functional-group families while changing ring frameworks.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Support moves that retain intact polar groups and their attachment context across meaningful scaffold alternatives, so familiar functional-group families remain accessible during structural changes. Use observed feedback to determine where retention helps; neither adding the same group everywhere nor preserving every incumbent ring is implied.

method_name: Mol GA: rank-selected de novo graph evolution
method_thesis: Anchor the root in Mol GA: maintain a population of oracle-evaluated molecular graphs, sample breeding parents across high-ranked quantiles, generate new offspring through graph crossover and atom/bond mutations, and update survivors greedily after each observation. These are the proposal and selection mechanisms described by [Tripp and Hernández-Lobato (2023)](https://arxiv.org/html/2310.09267v1). Start from the supplied initial observations and incorporate newly evaluated offspring immediately, following the evaluator's announced batching. Repeated graph edits and recombination create an evolving search space; no corpus ranking, stored molecule library, pretrained model, or fixed candidate enumeration is needed. The causal hypothesis is that direct selection on task-local scores concentrates successive structural changes around improving molecules quickly enough to raise the final best observed score. The published evidence concerns a larger-budget AUC-Top-10 setting, so its transfer to this benchmark's final Top-1 objective remains a hypothesis.

activation_observables.measurement: Independently enumerate the registered attachment/root/target options on the exact input of every actual change_bond call. Require zero immediate atom-count, bond-count and molecular-formula deltas, intact branch composition/internal graph, and unchanged source aromatic atoms and ring edges. Require a changed canonical nonisomeric molecular identity for novel direct positional products; symmetry-equivalent products remain ordinary duplicates. Track whether the relocated attachment remains present in the final emitted graph using the recorded immediate graph and later trace context; ancestry alone is not proof of retention. The Parent has 69600 pool entries from 75607 outer attempts and complete pools; new choices may change later retries and search trajectories, which must remain visible. Join evaluated relocation-bearing descendants to actual generating-parent scores and accepted feedback, reporting best-parent beats, child-minus-best-parent scores, incumbent gains, later survival and realized reuse separately from unchanged-operator cohorts. Distinguish a direct final relocation from an earlier relocated ancestor and separate one- from multi-atom branches. Compare the complete paired task/seed endpoints and macro score with the Parent using the supplied minimum effect. A pool-only positional alternative has no score; unselected menu choices and displaced legacy products receive no invented oracle labels. A final-score gain with no useful accepted relocation ancestry cannot be credited to the proposed ancestry pathway.

applicability_conditions: The new option requires a complete acyclic, single-attachment branch on a neutral aromatic carbon and an adjacent eligible aromatic C-H. Ring-bearing substituents, connecting linkers with two attachments, distant target positions and locally annotated roots are excluded. No broader aromatic rearrangement or stereo-assignment mechanism is included.

One-atom branches and multi-atom branches share the same construction rule and are reported separately. The earlier experiment's four evaluated multi-atom moves all lost to their sources, so intact-group retention is not treated as prior evidence of favorable score.

The Parent source audit uses only original first-parent graphs of recorded pool members. It does not reconstruct hidden failed inner draws, identify which bond those historical draws selected, establish alternative-product novelty, or supply counterfactual objective values.

The changed applicability condition is the Parent's existing learned selection over fresh surplus pools followed by accepted-survivor breeding. The prior relocation trial used a single-current-state inverse-memory walk; none of its relocated groups won a batch. The same chemical move may still be poorly selected or fail survivor competition here.

Immediate relocation conserves formula and the complete branch/ring framework. Subsequent inherited mutations or crossover may change these properties, and a successful ancestry trace does not guarantee that a particular attachment survived. No global size target, donor restriction or chemical-admission filter is introduced.

Existing reactive bonds, unusual ring topologies and incomplete stereochemistry can persist in a conserved branch or framework. Positional accessibility, stable identity and valid graph construction do not establish favorable geometry, synthesis or general chemical quality.

Expanded selected-bond menus change probabilities among their legacy alternatives and can alter later stochastic history even with the same number of RNG calls. Whole-panel paired comparisons assess the complete changed method; selected-stream subgroup outcomes cannot assign labels to unchosen options or isolate an individual move's score contribution.

approach.method_basis: The Parent breeds fresh molecular graphs from accepted, score-ranked survivors using fragment crossover and local atom or bond edits. A fingerprint Gaussian process learned from all earlier accepted scores selects each evaluation batch by correlated posterior draws over the fresh pool. The Parent also verifies stable canonical identities before pool admission, normalizing confirmed aliases without replacing the checked graph. Its bond-change move alters bond order; it has no direct move that shifts an intact side group to a neighboring aromatic position while keeping the whole molecule's composition.
approach.novelty: Add intact pendant-branch relocation to the existing bond-change menu: detach an acyclic side group from an aromatic carbon and reconnect that same group to an adjacent aromatic carbon bearing a hydrogen. This exposes substitution-position alternatives while preserving the group, ring framework and formula. Earlier siblings changed parent allocation or survival, protected all first-parent rings, redirected halogen growth, protected carbonyl atoms, or stabilized identity keys. None tested this positional move in their fresh graph pools. A different graph-walk lineage evaluated ten such moves but retained none; this experiment tests whether the Parent's existing learned pool selection can put a useful positional alternative into accepted breeding ancestry.

finding_summary.headline: Positional moves reached useful breeding ancestry, but the panel score fell slightly
finding_summary.insights:
The fresh-pool selector and accepted-survivor breeder can carry a useful positional edit into later ancestry, resolving the earlier graph-walk experiment's absence of retained relocation winners. The demonstrated benefit is narrow: two of 13 evaluated one-atom moves improved their parents, while none of seven evaluated multi-atom moves did. Keeping a larger branch intact therefore establishes access to positional alternatives without establishing better scores. A score-neutral methyl relocation also entered extensive later ancestry, so immediate parent improvement and later usefulness are different observations.

Two final-best molecules have recorded relocation ancestry, but subsequent edits and crossover prevent assigning their endpoint gains to a conserved moved group. Changing the option menu also changes the search path, so the paired panel measures the complete method; it supplies no scores for unselected alternatives. The molecular assessment still finds concentrated aromatic polycycles, reactive heteroatom bonds, strained ring arrangements and unspecified stereochemistry. Local formula and ring conservation did not resolve those chemical limitations, and the panel loss leaves the registered score-benefit expectation refuted even though construction, evaluated positional access and useful breeding ancestry are confirmed.
finding_summary.results:
All 368 sampled branch reconnections preserved the registered atom and bond counts, molecular formula, branch composition and aromatic ring framework. Of the 365 moves that changed molecular identity, 362 reached pools and 20 were evaluated with the relocated attachment still present. The evaluated set contained 13 one-atom and seven multi-atom branches. Two moves beat their generating parents; both moved fluorine. Sixteen evaluated products survived their batch, and 14 were chosen as breeding parents 979 times across 972 later attempts. One fluorine shift increased its source score from 0.382775 to 0.394039, raised the incumbent, and was reused in 444 attempts with 85 later accepted descendants. Every evaluated multi-atom move scored below its best generating parent.

Mean final-best score across three seeds was 0.542797, versus 0.544374 for the Parent: a paired change of -0.001577, which misses the required +0.002 gain. Seed variation decreased from a population standard deviation of 0.013310 to 0.004718, but the paired seed changes were mixed. All 435 pools filled to 160 candidates and all 4,350 proposed evaluations were accepted. Stable identity bookkeeping was preserved; its inherited guard rejected seven unstable representations before pool admission.
